standing_domain.text: \paragraph{Standing torus-fibration setting.} The ambient space is a smooth compact complex threefold $Y$ with $b_1(Y)=b_2(Y)=0$, and $f:Y\to B$ is proper and surjective with connected fibres and smooth general fibre a complex two-torus. Every statement below concerning an irreducible support uses its actual full fibre $mS$, normalization and resolution. The global assertions expressly retaining the hypothesis that every support is irreducible or has normal crossings are used with that hypothesis. Constructions and comparison examples with different Betti numbers state their own assumptions.

targets.label: night:P4.24
targets.statement:
\begin{proposition}[P4.24]\hypertarget{tag-02WW}{}\label{night:P4.24}\label{stmt:P4.24}
\StatementRecord{night:P4.24}{proved}{02WW}{the definitions and constructions stated in the proof}

In the standing torus-fibration setting of this section, let $S$ be an irreducible
singular fibre support with smooth normalization $T$.
If the minimal model of $T$ is a Hopf surface, then
$T$ is already minimal. The reduced conductor on $T$
and its reduced image in $S$ are disjoint unions of
smooth elliptic curves. Each map between their
components is a finite unramified covering, and
$e(S)=0$.
\end{proposition}

targets.label: night:P4.25
targets.statement:
\begin{proposition}[P4.25]\hypertarget{tag-02WX}{}\label{night:P4.25}\label{stmt:P4.25}
\StatementRecord{night:P4.25}{proved}{02WX}{\SeriesRef{night:P4.16}, \SeriesRef{night:P4.20}, \SeriesRef{night:P4.6}, \SeriesRef{night:P4.8}}

Every semi-log-canonical reduced fibre support in
Part~4.2 has normal crossings. In particular, let
$\rho:T\to N\to S$ be a resolution of the normalization
of an irreducible support, and let $D$ be the integral
divisor defined by
$\omega_T(D)\simeq\rho^*\omega_S$. When this actual
divisor is reduced and has normal crossings, $S$
has normal crossings, its normalization is smooth,
and P4.6--P4.8 apply.
\end{proposition}
